preamble: Depalatalization of a palatal stop [c] to a velar [k] is best known from the centum branches of Indo-European, where the Proto-Indo-European palatovelar *ḱ, conventionally interpreted as a palatal or palatalized velar stop, merged with plain velar *k. The merger happened in Italic, Celtic, Hellenic, Tocharian and Anatolian (in part), contrasting with satem branches where *ḱ became a sibilant (Sanskrit śatám, Avestan satəm, Lithuanian šimtas). Germanic also merged *ḱ with *k but then shifted it to h by Grimm's law.

examples.to: Proto-Tocharian *känte > Tocharian B kante, Tocharian A känt
examples.note: Tocharian, though spoken in the East, is a centum branch.

sources: Fortson, B. W. (2010). Indo-European Language and Culture: An Introduction (2nd ed.). Wiley-Blackwell. https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Indo-European+Language+and+Culture%3A+An+Introduction%2C+2nd+Edition-p-9781405188968
